key_insight: RubricsTree turns open-ended personal health agent evaluation into a scalable, expert-aligned checklist of clinically verifiable rubrics.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical evaluation-and-training infrastructure for health AI systems that need auditability, consistency, and continuous improvement at product scale.
method: Builds a hierarchical taxonomy of 100+ atomic Boolean rubrics aligned with clinical expertise.
Iteratively evolves the rubric set from 4,000 real user queries using human-in-the-loop curation led by an experienced physician.
Uses an adaptive router to activate only the relevant rubric subset for each query and auto-weight the scores.
evidence_signal: In meta-evaluation, RubricsTree outperformed a strong baseline on expert alignment for hard open-ended queries, penalized degraded responses more reliably, and improved HealthBench performance by up to ~66% relative across Gemini, GPT, and Qwen families when used as instructions, feedback, or rewards.
watch_item: The framework depends on high-quality expert curation and domain-specific rubric maintenance, so coverage and clinical validity may need ongoing updates as medical practice and user needs evolve.
paper_title: RubricsTree: Scalable and Evolving Open-Ended Evaluation of Personal Health Agents across Health Memory and Medical Skills
